cards.title: Incubation Mixing and Unstirred-Water-Layer Effects in Hepatocyte Clearance Assays
cards.claim: Mixing conditions can influence apparent permeability and measured intrinsic clearance in hepatocyte incubations. The cited analysis proposes unstirred-water-layer (UWL) effects as one explanation for interlaboratory differences, particularly for permeable compounds; rotatable-bond count was used as an indirect property correlate, not a measurement of permeability.
conditions: Hepatocyte incubation results from different protocols or laboratories are compared.
Mixing, assay duration and compound-property information are available or explicitly missing.
required_inputs: Incubation protocol, shaking/static conditions and cell preparation.
CLint values with units, replicate uncertainty and source provenance.
Measured permeability when available; rotatable bonds and other physicochemical descriptors labeled as indirect descriptors.
limitations: The compilation did not directly establish UWL causality for every compound.
No universal shaking correction, fold increase or permeability value follows from rotatable-bond count.
cards.downstream_use: Retain mixing conditions in IVIVE data qualification and represent unexplained protocol differences as uncertainty rather than silently pooling results.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
